decisions.briefing: Stocks slipped today, with the NASDAQ down 0.9% and the S&P 500 down 0.7%, a mildly negative day with no clear direction. Cash is $445.88, which is under the $500 minimum for a new buy, so there is no room to add a position. TTWO looks strong, with all five buy signals, but we are holding all seven positions and letting the automatic profit targets and stop-losses handle exits.

market_education.summary_en: Stocks drifted lower today, with the NASDAQ down 0.9% and the S&P 500 down 0.7%. Growth and tech stocks fell more than the broader market. Some semiconductor names were especially weak: NVDA traded at oversold levels on heavy volume. No news headlines were supplied for this session, so we can't pin today's move on a specific event. A drop this size usually reflects traders taking profits and trimming risk rather than a real change in the market's direction.
market_education.summary_zh: 美股今日走低，納指跌0.9%，標普500指數跌0.7%。增長股及科技股跌幅大於大市，部分半導體股走勢尤其疲弱，NVDA在大成交量下跌至超賣水平。本節未有提供新聞標題，因此難以將今日走勢歸因於單一事件。這種幅度的回調，通常反映資金獲利回吐及減低風險，而非市況方向出現實質轉變。

daily_lesson.explanation_en: Cash drag is the return you give up by holding cash instead of investments. With $445 sitting idle, that small slice of the portfolio earns nothing while stocks move. Still, when the amount is too small to buy a proper position and the market is falling, holding the cash is reasonable. A small, deliberate cash buffer is better than forcing a poor trade.
daily_lesson.explanation_zh: 「現金拖累」是指持有現金而非投資所放棄的回報。組合中閒置約445美元，這部分資金不會隨股市升跌而產生回報。不過，當金額太小、不足以建立合適倉位，而市況又正在下跌時，保留現金是合理做法。刻意保留少量現金緩衝，總好過勉強進行一宗差勁的交易。
